name: Mandinka
notes: Mandinka (Mandingo), the Manding branch of Mande, spoken in Casamance (Senegal), the Gambia (where it is co-official) and Guinea-Bissau. This spec covers the official Latin orthography (Senegal/Gambia literacy conventions, following Creissels & Sambou 2013 'Le mandinka (Sénégal, Gambie, Guinée-Bissau)'); Mandinka is also written in an older and more widely used Ajami (Arabic-script) tradition and, in Guinea-Bissau and neighbouring areas, in N'Ko — neither is modelled here (a spec is one script at a time; AGENTS.md §7 does not require a spec to cover every script a language has ever used). CONSONANTS: 19 phonemes /p b t d tʃ dʒ k ɡ m n ɲ ŋ f s h w r l j/, written ⟨p b t d c j k g m n ñ ŋ f s h w r l y⟩; the letters v, x, z, q are not used (Wikipedia, 'Mandinka language', Orthography section). /p/ and /ɡ/ are attested mainly in French loanwords per Creissels & Sambou; the digraph analysis follows the Manding convention (shared with Wolof/Bambara-adjacent literacy) of writing the palatal affricates as single letters ⟨c⟩ /tʃ/ and ⟨j⟩ /dʒ/ rather than digraphs. VOWELS: five qualities /i e a o u/ (Mandinka lost the ATR-based 7-vowel system some sister Manding languages like Maninka retain), each with a phonemic length contrast written by doubling the vowel letter (⟨aa ee ii oo uu⟩); doubled-vowel keys earn their place under AGENTS.md §2 test 2 (one long vowel nucleus, not two short vowels in sequence) and are cited directly rather than derived, since a bare concatenation rule would also mis-fire on true VV hiatus sequences the language does not orthographically distinguish from length in this simplified treatment. There are no nasal vowels; nasality surfaces instead as a coda /ŋ/ that assimilates to a following consonant's place (Wikipedia; not modelled as separate allophone keys since the assimilation is phonetic detail below the broad-IPA grain this spec targets, consistent with how coda nasal assimilation is handled elsewhere in this repo, e.g. Bantu prenasalised-stop specs). TONE: Mandinka has a two-tone (high/low) system with a well-documented set of morphologically-conditioned tone changes on the definite suffix -o (Wikipedia; Creissels & Sambou). The standard Latin orthography does not mark tone at all, so — matching the convention this repo already applies to other unmarked-tone Latin orthographies (e.g. Temne `tem`) — no tone is emitted here; there is no orthographic tone mark to key on, so this is a genuine engine/orthography gap rather than a spelling omission. GEMINATION: word-medial geminate consonants are attested (e.g. /pp tʃtʃ dʒdʒ kk ll mm nn ɲɲ/, Wikipedia) but are not distinguished from single consonants in the standard orthography (no doubled-consonant convention parallel to the vowels), so no separate geminate keys are asserted.

ancestors.notes: Mande (Glottolog mand1469) — Mandinka belongs to the Manding branch of West Mande. No Manding-branch or Mande-internal clade node exists yet in this dataset for Central Mande/Manding, so the language attaches directly to the top Mande node rather than inventing an intermediate node for a single descendant; a Manding-branch node is warranted once a second Manding language (e.g. Bambara `bam`, Maninka, Dyula) is added.
